title: Tool Contract Harmony Adapter: unify OpenAI-style tools and legacy function surface
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers use a mix of OpenAI-style "tools" (name + JSON schema params) and our legacy function invocation surface (function name + positional/keyword args). In the wild we see misrouted calls, name collisions, and inconsistent parameter serializations leading to runtime errors and poor developer experience.

Goal: Implement a compatibility adapter in the runtime that normalizes incoming tool/function calls to a single internal contract while preserving both input shapes and observability. The adapter should: normalize names and aliases, translate parameter encodings (JSON Schema <-> legacy arg list), preserve structured output semantics, and provide opt-in compatibility modes for customers who need strict OpenAI or legacy behavior.

Why now: Increased customers adopting OpenAI-style tool metadata in prompts and our recent structured-output improvements require a single, well-documented compatibility layer to reduce regressions and support deterministic rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime accepts both 'tools' and 'functions' fields on the API and routes to the same adapter when compatibility_mode is enabled.
- Name collisions are resolved according to the name-resolution policy and logged with a deprecation warning.
- Parameter translation passes schema-based round-trip tests for at least 100 common tool signatures.
- End-to-end smoke tests for chat streaming + tool call + structured output succeed under hosted and dedicated configurations.
- Metrics emitted: tool_call_resolved (success/failure/ambiguity), name_normalization_count, param_translation_latency.
- Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and linked from SDKs.
technical_notes:
Design overview: add runtime module 'tool_harmony_adapter' with three components:
1) Name Normalizer: deterministic canonicalization rules (lowercase, strip non-alphanum, replace spaces and dots with underscores). Support explicit aliasing via registry. Collision policy: prefer exact legacy function match, otherwise use latest-versioned tool by model compatibility; emit telemetry and warning header.
2) Param Translator: two translation paths. (a) OpenAI tools -> internal func call: validate tool.params against provided JSON Schema, flatten to ordered args according to 'param_order' metadata or alphabetical fallback. (b) Legacy function -> OpenAI tool contract: synthesize a JSON object following the tool schema and attach it to the call metadata. Keep original raw payload in runtime logs for debugging.
3) Output Normalizer: when function/tool returns structured data or a 'tool_call' with content, normalize to Redwood structured-output envelope (type + body + metadata) and preserve any 'tool_response' raw bytes for audit.

Implementation details: adapter lives as a middleware at request-routing layer. For streaming responses use an async translator that can buffer the tool invocation result without blocking token streaming for the model; emit a streaming sentinel message when the runtime is invoking external tool. Add feature flag 'compatibility_mode' with values 'off'|'openai-legacy'|'strict-openai'. Default 'off' for now.

Backward compatibility: if compatibility_mode is off, current behavior unchanged. When on, the adapter reconciles both fields but maintains headers to indicate which translation occurred.

Telemetry: add new metrics and logs as described in acceptance criteria. Instrumentation must be present before behavioral rollout.
migration_notes:
- SDK changes: add 'compatibility_mode' option to client constructors and a small helper to register aliases.
- Document deprecated legacy names that will be canonicalized; provide a 3-month deprecation window with header warnings.
- Provide a small CLI tool (python) to scan repos for tool/function name usages and suggest aliases.
- Offer migration checklist for customers on Dedicated/Private that includes testing endpoints and toggling compatibility_mode in a canary ring.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): deploy adapter behind feature flag to 5% of hosted traffic and to an internal Dedicated pool. Monitor metrics for 1 week.
Phase 2 (usage opt-in): release SDK with compatibility_mode opt-in flags and document migration. Enable opt-in for selected enterprise customers.
Phase 3 (wide opt-in): enable compatibility_mode as an opt-in tenant-level setting in the Console and run a compatibility sweep.
Phase 4 (opt-out deprecation): after 3 months of broad opt-in and no major regressions, consider making 'openai-legacy' available as default for new tenants only.
Rollback: disable feature flag and revert name registry changes; adapter is stateless so rollback should be fast but requires invalidation of alias cache on edge nodes.
open_questions: Should the adapter attempt best-effort coercion for scalar-to-array mismatches or fail-fast?
How do we version tool schemas in the registry and choose the correct schema when multiple versions exist?
Do we provide user-facing request/response headers indicating translation occurred (for SDKs and customers)?
What quota/accounting implications exist when a translated tool triggers an external provider call?
decisions: Use deterministic name normalization (strip punctuation, lowercase, replace non-alphanum with underscore) as default; allow explicit alias registry to override.
Translate tool.params using JSON Schema-driven translators; fall back to alphabetic ordering when param_order is not provided.
Emit a streaming sentinel event when adapter invokes an external tool so client SDKs can surface 'tool is running' state while model output is paused.
updates: 2025-01-10: Initial ticket created after onboarding call with Solutions SEs who reported 3 customer regressions due to name collisions.
2025-01-15: Prototype name normalizer landed in internal branch; early tests show 98% match rate for common tool names. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/813
2025-01-22: Param translator prototype able to round-trip 60/100 curated tool schemas. Remaining failures from ambiguous optional arrays—raising question about coercion policy.
2025-02-01: Design review with PM and DX. Agreed on streaming sentinel and metrics. Added 'compatibility_mode' options to SDK roadmap.
2025-02-03: Started implementation of output normalizer and added metrics scaffolding. Hooked up telemetry for name_normalization_count.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: (1) name normalization edge cases and alias registry API, (2) param translator round-trip test coverage and failure modes, (3) streaming behavior during external tool invocation. Please validate telemetry names and alert thresholds in the rollout plan.
